transcript.text: t/d keeps cutting out after 10 mins then starts again if i leave it. vent hose goes out the window. pls help

Please switch the dryer off, unplug it and let it cool down first. A blocked filter can cause overheating, triggering a safety cut-out. Once safe to touch, please check the fluff filter located in the door opening; note that heat-pump models may also have a second filter at the bottom. You might find our guide image helpful for locating these parts. Was it full of fluff (and is it clean now), or was it already clean?
[Helpful to see: image "Where the lint filter is" — The fluff/lint filter sits in the door opening or just inside the rim. Lift it out and clear the fluff after every load. Typical layout — your dryer may differ.]
its ok i clean the filter every time. cabinet gets really hot before it stops tho

Thanks for letting us know about the overheating issue. Please switch the dryer off, unplug it and let it cool down first. Then check the vent hose at the back: ensure it is short, has no kinks or squashed sections, and is clear of fluff all the way to the outside vent. Was it kinked, squashed or blocked (and is it sorted), or was it already clear?
ok just looked. i pushed the dryer back further recently and the hose is all squashed and kinked behind it. theres fluff in the folds too

Thanks for checking that. Since you found a blockage, clearing the duct is the next step and may well sort the issue. Please switch the dryer off, unplug it and let it cool down first. Then check the vent hose at the back: ensure it is short, has no kinks or squashed sections, and is clear of fluff all the way to the outside vent. Was it kinked, squashed or blocked (and is it sorted), or was it already clear?
yeah like i said its squashed and kinked with fluff in the folds. ill pull the dryer out a bit and straighten it. anything else i should do?

Thanks for confirming the vent hose is clear. Please run a normal drying programme and stay nearby to monitor it. If the electrics trip or you smell burning, stop it immediately, leave it switched off, and tell me. Does it run right through now, or still stop part way?
